tvar.module: /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R3/tvar/variants.py. It is pure numpy and imports in both the CAD venv and Blender's python; it reads only T3/shape.py. API: VIDS = ("0","A","B","C"); params(vid); section(vid,u) -> (c, ti, to, w, ni, no); profile(vid,u) -> (half_width, half_thick_inner, half_thick_outer), where both half thicknesses are measured from the seam/equator x = seam_x(vid,u) and not from x = 0, so thickness = inner + outer; faces(vid,u) -> (x of inner face, x of outer face, seam x) on the centre line; thickness(vid,u); pebble_rows(vid,nu,nth,inset=0) -> (rows, top, bot), the same tuple and u/theta sampling as v1geo.pebble_rows; pebble_cloud; inside_local(vid,P,inset) (same inset meaning as v1geo); half_rows(vid,'vonk'|'vnut',nu,nth,gap=0.25) gives closed half solids with the seam gap, for rendering or export; tip_plane_local(vid); to_world(P,vid,dx=-1.0,sx=1), to_local, dir_world, swing(Q,deg) and swing_matrix(deg), all identical to armgeo/v1geo; subset_margin(vid). Section model: an asymmetric superellipse. The equator (seam) is at x = c(u) = -(1-ki)*H(u). The inner half has thickness ti = ki*ht and exponent ni; the outer half has to = ko*ht and exponent no; the half width is w = kw*hw, with (hw, ht) the approved T3 arm_profile. H = ht for u in [u1, 0.5], so the inner face on the centre line stays exactly at -ht there. Towards both tips H is smoothstep-blended to a constant, so the tips follow the slimmer body. Self-test (python variants.py): variant "0" matches the v1geo rows and the world placement to 1.6e-13 (assert < 0.01). Helper scripts in the same folder: chk_variants.py -> chk_variants.json, room.py -> room.json, chk_head.py -> chk_head.json, scene_tvar.py (copy of v2_scene.py with the variant arms; shots front / hero / heroarm / armfront / side / top / zoom, plus --vids), sheet_tvar.py.

tvar.look_notes:
How I read the complaint: in the front view the outer cover takes half the visible arm width (11.6 of 23.6 mm). In the hero view the raised arm shows a broad, flat outer oval (33.6 wide).

Strategy in all three variants:
- The arm gets thinner from the outside. The outer cover is a flatter dome: 11.5 -> 7.1 / 6.3 / 5.3 at the joint. In the front view the cover band becomes 7.2 / 6.3 / 5.3 instead of 11.6.
- The inner face stays, so the arm sits just as close to the torso as now (3.70 rest gap, 2.78 front-view gap).
- In B and C the inner half also thins and the seam (the equator, which is also the widest fore-aft line) moves inwards. It is curved in B and C and still the clean parting line; A keeps the current planar seam.
- The fore-aft width is deliberately 5 / 10 / 15 % narrower. Without that, a thin arm becomes a wide flat paddle in the hero and side views ('ruka pôsobí široká'), and the narrower width also gives the subset guarantee for the thinner inner half.
- In B and C both tips move inwards with the body. Without this the outer contour of B and C was a straight blade line (the first iteration looked like a leaf or feather).
- Black tip on the inner lower front: same plane normal as v1geo, with the plane point moved onto the new seam (u 0.86 / 0.85 / 0.84) so the black patch keeps a similar size.
- Splay 12 and swing 3 are unchanged.

Verdict from the previews:
- A still reads as the approved R01 pebble, only with a visibly thinner outer cover. It is the safest option and needs the joint stack about 3.4 shorter.
- B is in my view the best balance: clearly slim, still a rounded pebble, and the seam runs near the outer edge in the front view, much like the rim line on the R01 arm.
- C is about as slim as it can go: it reads as a slim leaf or flipper and the rounded inner shoulder at the top dominates. It is OK as the extreme option but less R01-like.

Joint consequence (computed, room.json): with a 1.2 wall, an r 12.7 hub fits up to x 67.8 now, 64.2 in A, 60.9 in B and 57.6 in C. The B1+ in-arm clutch (to x 67.6) fits only the current arm. B and C need the clutch moved into the torso or made much shorter.

Render caveats:
- The visible black spigot is the v2 'zatka' STL from img_v2 (read only), not the B1+ part.
- A dark core inside each arm is visible only through the 0.5 seam. It stands in for the internal lip, so the seam reads as a dark line, as in the approved renders.
- No hub or internals are modelled.
- The previews are 500 px, 16 samples, 3 threads.

options.name_sk: B1+ naplocho: 6700 + podložka M14 okolo ložiska, magnety 5×1
options.description: Same functions as B1+ (6700 on the plug seat, magnetic slip clutch, two-sided hidden stop, removable arm), repackaged three ways: (1) the steel friction washer is a DIN 125 M14 (ID 15 = 6700 OD) slipped over and epoxied onto the 6700 outer ring, so the washer is radially nested AROUND the bearing (friction face 0.3 beyond the bearing face); (2) thin 5x1 magnets in a 1.45 mm disc; (3) the M4 head is recessed 1.6 mm in a counterbore of the seat (DIN 912 M4x16). No lip ring is needed: when the arm is pulled outward the washer pushes the disc, so retention comes from the drive-hub press fit, as in B1+.
options.parts_in_arm: 6700ZZ, x 54.6..58.6 on the D10 seat; its inner ring rests on a step of the stop lug. DIN 125 M14 15x28x2.5 washer in ZINC-PLATED STEEL (not A2), x 56.4..58.9. Printed hub, part of A_vnut: bearing bore plus backing r 7.5..14.3, x 55.2..56.4. Stop rib r 5.3..8.5, x 52.8..54.3, 32.7 deg. Printed drive hub: ring pressed on the M4 head (x 58.9..61.0), cap with a 3 AF key (to 62.2), disc r 14.25 at x 58.9..60.35 with 10 pockets D5.1x1.2 at r 10.5 (web 1.5) behind a 0.25 skin. 4-9 NdFeB 5x1 N38.
options.parts_changed_in_torso: Plug (zátka) reprint only. Seat D10 shortened 59.5 -> 58.6 with a D7.6 counterbore (x 56.5..58.6, wall 1.2) for the head. Stop lug reshaped to r 5.0..6.7, x 52.5..54.3, plus a step r 5.0..5.5 to x 54.6. Arm shaft DIN 912 M4x16 instead of M4x20 (head x 57..61, tip x 41.0, full thread in the gear). A1/A2, gear, pinion, servo, column, D13 ring and arm hole are unchanged, so the arm-torso gap is unchanged.
options.envelope: x_outer >= 63.70 for r 0..4.7 (key cap 62.2 + 0.3 + 1.2); x_outer >= 61.85 for r 4.7..14.25 (disc 60.35 + 1.5). Governing spot: disc rim r 14.25, front-top. Shape variants: 0 fits (+0.95). A fails: the r 14 washer is only 0.64 from the inner surface fore-aft (-0.56), because A is 5 % narrower. B -1.14 and C -3.34 also fail. Stand-ins: kt 0.85 fits (+0.80), kt 0.70 fails (-0.23).
options.rules_ok: No metal work: yes. DIN 912 M4x16 8.8 zinc is a Hornbach item. 6700ZZ is already used by B1+ (bearing shops; the fixer notes 6800 is easier to buy). DIN 125 M14 zinc is a fastener-shop item: verify it is zinc steel, not A2, and magnetic. 5x1 N38 is sold on the Kaufland.cz marketplace and by Enes PL, but is less common than 5x2. Printed walls >= 1.2: yes, except the 0.25 friction skin, same concept as B1+. Sliding clearances >= 0.30: yes (checker). Cover wall >= 1.2: yes.
options.strength_and_function: Clutch, 5x1 N38 through the 0.25 skin: 0.45-0.64 N per magnet, 0.0012-0.0027 N.m per magnet at r 10.5. Fixer window 0.0082-0.0113: 4-9 of 10 pockets, in all cases. Brief window 0.0124-0.0170: 7-9 (mid) or 5-6 (high); the pessimistic case (F low, mu 0.25) needs 11 > 10, so use 5x1 N52 there. Balanced counts: any count except 1 and 3. Spacer factors 0.68 / 0.49. Stop 2.1 mm2: homing 1.35 MPa, 3 N tip push 17.1 MPa (B1+ 16.2), rib root 4.9 MPa. Seat under L5: 9.7 MPa in the A2 zone (same as B1+), 5.5 MPa at the counterbore. 6700 under L5: F/C0 about 0.27. Washer bond 0.03 MPa. Key 1.3 MPa. Retention about 7-32 N after relaxation (B1+ 13-60), scaled estimate. Tilt threshold 0.5-1.5 N at the tip, then <= 0.73 mm.
options.risks: The r 14.25 disc and washer sit near the fore-aft edge, so any narrower shape fails (A, B). Lower press-fit retention (grip 2.1 instead of 4.0). Availability of the M14 washer and the 5x1 magnets. The brief's torque window is only met with N52 in the pessimistic case.
options.verified_by_own_calc: Geometry fit, min thickness, envelope, stop gaps (0.56 at -45, 0.51 at +135, contact at -51 / +140.5), clearances, clutch counts and stress hand calcs: my own. Magnet force: my re-implementation of the B1 model, calibrated to 5x2. The absolute 5x1 force, mu, washer saturation, press-fit retention and bearing C0 are NOT verified.

options.description: The clutch moves into the torso drive line. The arm keeps the 6700 on the seat, the B1+-type stop, and a printed hub keyed rigidly on the recessed DIN 912 M4x16 head (hex 3 AF + press ring), with a web over the bearing. Result: the torso has no room for the clutch.

options.parts_changed_in_torso: Would need a slip clutch at the servo coupler, on the vertical shaft, or between the gear and the M4. Measured room (fixer's free map minus the B1+ column fill): around the vertical axis at coupler height (z -43.75..-33.75), the largest full circle is only r 4.5-5.0. It is limited by the column fill bands at y 7.5 / -8.5 and the neck pan/lift sweep at x about 34.5. The existing coupler already uses r 4.5 over z -43.5..-35.5, and above z -33.5 the side-cap notch leaves r 2. Servo-side torque is 0.0083-0.0113 N.m (brief) or 0.0055-0.0075 (fixer). A magnetic clutch: not one 5 mm magnet fits within r 4.5 beside the hex shaft (needs a disc of r >= 7-8). A spring friction clutch: assortment spring, closed internal loop so the pinion sees no axial force, 11-16 N preload at r_eff 2.8. It needs about 8.5-9 mm above the horn; about 6 mm is available. mech.summary:
**What makes the arm thick (B1+ / M1).** The arm-side stack (6700 -> M10 washer -> magnet disc r 11 -> lip/wall r 12.7 at x 67.6) needs the outer surface at x >= 67.4 for r <= 10.4 and x >= 68.8 for r 10.4..12.7. The arm's inner skin on the axis is at x 49.645. Result: a minimum of 22.8 mm at the joint, against today's 23.0 (margin 0.16, matching the judge's 1.36 wall).

**Why it costs so much.** The arm is splayed 12 deg and is a pebble, so the room for a part that is round about the shoulder axis shrinks by about 0.4 mm per mm of radius on both faces. The worst spots are straight above the axis (top) and at the fore-aft edges. Every large-radius part placed far outboard costs thickness.

**Options:**
- **M2 (B1+ flat, all functions kept).** 6700 + DIN 125 M14 washer nested around the bearing, 5x1 magnets in a 1.45 mm disc, M4x16 head recessed in the seat. Only a plug reprint. Reaches 16.5 mm on kt stand-ins, but its r 14.25 disc fails the shape designer's narrower variants A and B.
- **M2b (recommended).** MR128 + DIN 125 M12, A2 moved into the ring, low-head DIN 7984 M4x20, seat D10 at the root and D8 under the bearing. Reaches 15.5 mm. Fits variant A (18.65) with 1.5 spare and variant B (15.54) with only 0.085 spare. Fits the brief's 0.0124-0.0170 N.m window except the pessimistic case (needs N52 magnets). Open points: DIN 7984 is a fastener-shop item, not Hornbach (borderline with the hardware-store rule); seat at about 8.5 MPa under L5.
- **M3 (clutch into the torso).** Does not fit. The free full circle around the vertical axis at coupler height is only r 4.5-5. No 5 mm magnet fits beside the shaft, and a spring clutch needs about 9 mm of height where about 6 mm exists. Even its bare arm side (bearing + keyed hub) needs 14.5 mm.
- **M4 (no mechanical stop, Hall homing).** Rejected. It saves about 1.5 mm of stack, but its r 14.25 disc still governs (14.75 mm) and it fails the narrow variants.

**Conclusion for the shape designer.** About 19 mm is easy (M2b, or M2 if the arm keeps its full fore-aft width). About 16 mm works only with M2b, and only just: ask for about 0.5 mm more outer surface directly above the shoulder axis at u about 0.18. 13 mm (variant C) cannot hold any joint that keeps the clutch, bearing and stop: the best with a clutch (M2b) is 2.9 mm short, and the version without a clutch in the arm (M3) is 1.9 mm short and has no room in the torso. The arm–torso gap does not change in any option, because the inner face, the hole and the D13 ring stay the same.

**Verified by my own computation:**
- Fits, envelopes, minimum thicknesses and clearances, with a checker validated against the B1+ judge numbers.
- Stop gaps and contacts.
- Magnet counts, using my re-implementation of the B1 magnet model.
- Stress hand calcs.
- Room in the torso, read from the fixer's free map (read only).

**Not verified:**
- Absolute pull of 5x1 magnets, friction coefficient, washer saturation, press-fit retention and bearing C0 values.
- Shop availability: these come from search snippets only.
- Hall sensing in M4.

**Window note.** The fixer has since lowered the clutch window to 0.0082-0.0113 N.m (R2c/oprava/final_B1plus_fix.json). M2 and M2b meet that window in all cases.

(a) Cover glued as a closed section: lateral 1.46 MPa, fore-aft 0.80 MPa, so OK (current arm 0.54 / 0.42). (b) Design case, cover on magnets, inner half alone: lateral 11.9 MPa at the hub edge u 0.40, FAILS the 6 MPa abuse limit (current arm 4.8 MPa), fore-aft 1.5 MPa. A 2.8 wall still gives 7.3 MPa. 1 m drop: 1.1 kg robot = 10.8 J against an elastic capacity at UTS of 0.05 J (C open, lateral) to 0.28 J (C closed); the current arm has 0.08 / 0.42 J. Neither arm survives a robot drop onto the arm by elasticity, and C has about 35-40 % less capacity. The arm dropped alone carries 0.14 J; that is a local contact problem I did not compute. images.notes:
I rendered and built all four sheets. I opened each final PNG with Read and fixed every overlap and overflow I found. Every sheet is 1400 px wide. The renders used 48 samples on 3 threads.

How it works:
- **Scenes:** scene_v3.py is a copy of R3/tvar/scene_tvar.py, which is the v2_scene.py lineage, so it uses the same materials, lights and cameras as v2. I added two new shots, 'armonly' (the arm alone in its local frame) and 'rezv' (sections with --plane v|h and --opt), plus save_cam for armfront and heroarm.
- **Sheets:** sheets_v3.py builds them.
- **Numbers:** nums_v3.py writes nums_v3.json.
- **Rerun:** render_final.sh and run_rez.sh redo the renders.
- **Writes:** nothing was written outside R3. Read-only sources were T4, B, T3, img_v1, img_v2 (T_bok_L stl_mod and the v2 zatka), R2c/img/work/stl_b (plug body, column and A1 for the torso side of the sections), R3/tvar and R3/mech/stl.

Checked by my own computation:
- **Thickness, width, halves:** the values from variants.py match chk_variants.json. I rounded from the precise values, not from the 2-decimal JSON. A's maximum thickness is 18.647, shown as 18,6, and C's is 12.547, shown as 12,5. The JSON's 18.65 and 12.55 would round up to 18,7 and 12,6.
- **Outer-cover band in the front view:** measured at the u 0.22 height it is 11.54 / 7.13 / 6.32 / 5.28. That equals the outer half at the joint to 0.1 mm, so the zoom labels show outer_half_at_joint (11,5 / 7,1 / 6,3 / 5,3). The designer's 11.6 / 7.2 figures differ by up to 0.07 mm. I did not put the 'of 23.6 visible' numbers on the sheet.
- **Thin spots:** a KD-tree from the governing part edge to the analytic skin reproduces the JSON exactly: 0/M1 1.361 at az 15.8, A/M2b washer 1.962 at az 186.75, B/M2b cap 1.585 at az 87, C/M2b −1.402 at az 87. Because of where they sit, the 0 and A spots are marked in the horizontal section and the B and C spots in the vertical one.
- **Margins and gaps** are taken from the fit/verification JSON: +0.16, +0.76, +0.085 (shown as 0,09) and −2.90. Rest gap 3.70 and minimum gaps 1.001, 1.11, 1.125 and 1.039 (verifier: A 1.104).

Not verified / caveats:
- **Torso side of the sections:** the plug body, column and A1 are the B1 meshes from R2c/img (close to B1+, simplified). The M2b screw shank and spacer sleeve inside the plug are plain cylinders from the stated dimensions (M4 tip x 38.9 / 40.0; sleeve Ø7/Ø5 between A1 and A2).
- **Shell walls:** the cover is drawn 1.2 mm thick, the minimum used by the fit rules (B needs ≤ 1.285 locally over the cap). The inner shell is 1.6 mm. The strength estimates assumed 1.6 everywhere.
- **Hub:** the printed hub is drawn merged with the inner shell. In variant 0 the M1 hub shows its real crossing past the seam.
- **Not drawn:** the cover magnets (they clash and must move), seam lips and print details.
- **Renderer workarounds:** exact booleans failed on a few self-intersecting shells, so I used the FLOAT solver as a fallback with the cap faces recoloured. In C, the parts that poke out are subtracted from the cover so the protrusion shows clearly.
- **Visible black ring** in the front/3D views is the v2 'zatka' STL (visual only). The arms have no hub or internals in those views. The dark core in the arm only shows through the seam.
- **C joint line on sheet 1:** it says the clutch would not fit in the torso either. That is the M3 author's measurement, which the verifier did not re-check; the footnote says 'spojka presunutá do trupu sa tam nezmestí'.
